question: Conversion of ethanol to ethanoic acid is catalysed by:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Alkaline KMnO4 and Acidified K2Cr2O7**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alkaline KMnO4 and Acidified K2Cr2O7** are commonly used oxidizing agents in organic chemistry.
 
• These reagents are effective in converting **ethanol (a primary alcohol) to ethanoic acid (a carboxylic acid)**.
 
• **Acidified K2Cr2O7** (Potassium dichromate) in **acidic medium** acts as a **powerful oxidizing agent**.
 
• **Alkaline KMnO4** (Potassium permanganate) in **basic medium** also acts as a **strong oxidizing agent**.
 
• The oxidation process involves the removal of hydrogen from the ethanol molecule and the addition of oxygen to form ethanoic acid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In the oxidation of ethanol to ethanoic acid, **ethanol is first oxidized to acetaldehyde**, and then further oxidized to ethanoic acid.
 
• Both alkaline KMnO4 and acidified K2Cr2O7 are strong oxidants that can facilitate the complete oxidation of ethanol.
 
• This reaction is an example of an oxidation-reduction (redox) reaction where ethanol loses electrons (is oxidized) and the oxidizing agent gains electrons (is reduced).
 
• These reagents are widely used in organic synthesis and analytical chemistry for various oxidation reactions.
